name: Rational-time lonely-runner certificates
description: construct() -> [p,q] of Python integers with 0<p<q<=1000000, representing time p/q. For relative speeds [1,3,4,7,11,18,29] from a stationary runner, maximize the minimum circular distance of (p/q)*v to an integer. Exact rational distances are retained in details; score is their floating serialization. One stationary runner and seven fixed relative integer speeds [1,3,4,7,11,18,29]; maximize the minimum distance at a rational time with denominator<=10^6. This lower-bound certificate does not optimize over all speed sets or prove a universal conjecture. The optimum is exactly 1/5, at t = 1/5; every breakpoint of the piecewise-linear objective has been checked, so this is a rediscovery task.

state_of_the_art.statement: For the speeds {1,3,4,7,11,18,29} the maximum over all times of the minimum distance is exactly 1/5, attained at t = 1/5 (no speed is a multiple of 5). The objective is piecewise linear with breakpoints at denominators dividing v_i + v_j or 2v_i. Checking every denominator up to 116 (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py) therefore proves optimality. The lonely runner conjecture predicts only 1/8 for seven speeds.
